subject: Archaeology
title: Isotope Analysis: You Are What You Eat
description: A quick, practical guide to Isotope Analysis: You Are What You Eat.

hook.text: Your bones record what you ate and where you grew up. Ancient skeletons carry the same chemical autobiography.

buildup.text: Strontium isotopes in tooth enamel match the geology of where a person grew up.

discovery.text: Carbon and nitrogen isotopes in bone reveal diet. High nitrogen means meat-heavy diets; high carbon-13 means marine food.

twist.text: The Amesbury Archer, found near Stonehenge, grew up in the Alps. He traveled 800 miles to England 4,000 years ago.

climax.text: Isotope analysis is rewriting migration history. People moved far more often in prehistory than anyone assumed.

punchline.text: Your teeth remember where you were born. Archaeology just learned to read them.

quiz.question: What did isotope analysis reveal about the Amesbury Archer?
options: He had a diet entirely of seafood despite living inland
He grew up in the Alps and traveled 800 miles to Stonehenge
He was the oldest known resident of Britain
